chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to a man: 'Make your heart a righteous companion, or a child that maintains ties [with parents]; make your deed a parent that you follow; make your self an enemy that you strive against; and make your wealth a loan that you will return.'
ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim view their heart, deeds, self, and wealth according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this profound teaching from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines a holistic framework for spiritual self-mastery by redefining the believer's relationship with their inner self, actions, and material possessions. This metaphorical structuring emphasizes that the heart must be a companion of virtue, deeds must be the guiding parent, the nafs is an adversary to be constantly fought, and wealth is merely a temporary deposit. This perspective aligns with the Shia emphasis on *mujahadat al-nafs* (striving against the self) as the core mechanism for achieving closeness to God.

en.hubeali: ‘Abu Abdullahasws said to a man: ‘Make your heart to be a righteous companion as a child would be grateful to its parents, and make your deed to be a father which you follow (cheerfully), and make your ‘Nafs’ (yourself) to be an enemy against which you wage a war, and make your wealth as a lease you will be returning’.
en.sarwar: 7. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) in a marfu’ manner from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.)

who has said the following to a man: “Make your heart a virtuous companion for yourself or like a child who does not fail to maintain good relations with parents. Consider your deeds as your father whom you follow, consider your soul as your enemy against whom you strive and consider your properties as borrowed for the safe return of which you are responsible.”
